newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Cairns Group nations meet to draw up WTO strategy.
newsitem.headline: Cairns Group nations meet to draw up WTO strategy.

text.p: The Cairns Group of agricultural exporting nations met Thursday to draw up a strategy for negotiations at the World Trade Organization (WTO) and to ratify its undertaking to improve access to markets.
The two-day ministerial meeting in Rio de Janeiro also marked the expansion of the group to include Paraguay, the first new member to join since it was founded in 1986.
"We are here today to set a path towards fundamental reform of the agricultural world," said the Tim Fisher, Australia's deputy prime minister and agriculture minister.
"We are also here to send a message to the world that the Cairns Group is absolutely determined to see that reform achieved," Fisher said in a speech.
The WTO is expected to begin negotiations over agriculture at the end of 1999.

"We need to decide in this meeting a wide-ranging strategy that we will adopt over the next 18 months with the final aim of ensuring we are prepared for a robust and serious start to negotiations in 1999," Fisher said.
Brazilian Foreign Minister Luiz Felipe Lampreia urged the European Union, the United States and Japan to reduce their barriers to agricultural imports.

The members of the Cairns Group, which includes Australia, Canada and New Zealand, account for about 20 percent of the world's agricultural exports. (( -- Julio Villaverde, Rio de Janeiro newsroom 5521 5074151))
